title: Decode, Refract, Drag & Morph
description: A staggered decode reveal, a real liquid-glass refraction filter, a text scramble, an elastic spring slider, and a morphing dialog.

drops.title: Character Decode Reveal
drops.description: Headline text splits into per-character spans that blur-and-lift into place on a cascading stagger as they scroll into view.
drops.concept: Every glyph starts blurred, offset, and invisible, then resolves via a shared CSS keyframe with a per-character animation-delay driven by a --i custom property. An IntersectionObserver flips animation-play-state from paused to running once the section enters the viewport, turning a pure-CSS effect into a scroll trigger.

interaction.mouse: Scroll to trigger each section's reveal
interaction.click: Use the Replay button to re-run
interaction.touch: Scroll on mobile triggers the same reveal

drops.title: Liquid Glass Dock
drops.description: A real SVG feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap filter refracts the backdrop through frosted glass — dock, pill nav, and card, no images.
drops.concept: An SVG <filter> chains feTurbulence (fractal noise) into feDisplacementMap to warp the backdrop like light bending through glass, then splits the result into red/blue channels with feOffset + feBlend for a subtle chromatic-fringe edge. Applied to any element via backdrop-filter: url(#liquidGlass), with a plain blur() fallback for browsers that can't parse SVG filter references in backdrop-filter.
drops.source: nikdelvin/liquid-glass — CSS + SVG recreation of Apple's Liquid Glass

interaction.mouse: Hover dock icons to magnify, tune sliders to reshape the refraction live
interaction.touch: Tap dock icons and nav links

drops.title: Scramble Decode Text
drops.description: Characters roll through random glyphs before locking into the real text — on load, on hover, and with a fully randomized lock order.
drops.concept: Each character gets a randomly-jittered reveal deadline (position-correlated for a left-to-right sweep, or fully randomized for a jitterier decode). On each tick, unrevealed characters are replaced with a random glyph from a selectable charset; once the frame counter passes a character's deadline it locks to the real value.

interaction.mouse: Hover the word row to decode each word
interaction.click: Replay buttons re-trigger the headline and stats
interaction.touch: Tap words on mobile to trigger the scramble

drops.title: Elastic Drag Slider
drops.description: Drag a thumb past the track's edge and it resists with a compressed rubber-band stretch, then springs back — plus a stepped, magnetic-snap variant.
drops.concept: While dragging, overflow past the track's bounds is compressed through a sigmoid decay function and capped at a max-overflow distance, producing a rubber-band stretch instead of a hard stop. On release, a hand-rolled spring integrator (stiffness/damping driven by requestAnimationFrame) eases the overflow back to zero, with a stepped variant that snaps to notches.

interaction.mouse: Drag any thumb past its track edge and release
interaction.click: Click anywhere on a track to jump

drops.title: Morphing View-Transition Dialog
drops.description: Tap a button and it morphs — same identity, new size and place — into a native <dialog>, powered by the View Transitions API.
drops.concept: document.startViewTransition() wraps the DOM mutation that opens/closes a native <dialog>. Right before the mutation, the shared view-transition-name is moved from the trigger button onto the dialog (and back again on close) so the browser's auto-generated morph animates between the button's screen rect and the dialog's centered rect, with the label kept as a separately-named element so text doesn't stretch.
drops.source: Rik Schennink (Pqina) — Animating the Dialog Element Using View Transitions

interaction.mouse: Click a trigger button to open, click outside or Close to dismiss
